transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-20
Start time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Li (Redwood SE), Jordan Kim (Redwood), Priya Nair (HelixWorks Dir ML), Tom Alvarez (HelixWorks Platform), Santiago Ruiz (HelixWorks SRE), Lea Wong (HelixWorks NLP)

Summary:
Quick sync on this week's POC runs: TTFT micro-sampling, streaming variance, sequence length matrix, and kernel selection notes. Confirmed some intermittent microbursts on the streaming path; discussed KV cache warmup and quantization tradeoffs.

Topics:
- TTFT micro-sampling results
- Streaming handoff variance
- Sequence length impact on kernel choice
- Actionable test plan and next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Ethan Park: ok everyone, thanks for joining, let's kick off. we're about 50 minutes. quick roll call?
[00:08] Priya Nair: hey yeah priya here, tom, santiago, lea all on too
[00:12] Tom Alvarez: yep
[00:15] Maya Li: great, so quick agenda, i'll run the TTFT micro-sample highlights then jordan will go into streaming variance, then we triage next steps
[00:25] Priya Nair: sounds good
[00:28] Maya Li: ok first slide, the micro-sampling. we ran the 1k synthetic traces with 8 token warmup and then measured first-token time across priorities. median improved about 18% with prefix prefetch enabled, 95th about 32% on our dev cluster, but we still see a thin tail around microbursts at 97-99p
[00:50] Lea Wong: that tail, is that correlated to seq len? we noticed longer inputs are worse
[00:55] Maya Li: yes, good point. the 2x seqlen tests showed 97p jumps. looks like kernel choice flips to the fallback path around 2k sequence for the model variant you're using
[01:12] Santiago Ruiz: when you say fallback path, do you mean a different attention kernel? I thought Redwood runtime picks kernels dynamically
[01:20] Jordan Kim: yeah runtime does pick, but there's a point where the preferred kernel for throughput has worse latency for small batch sizes; it can flip to a more conservative kernel which adds per-token overhead. that's the flip we observed
[01:36] Tom Alvarez: is that deterministic? we saw the flip at 1.9k seq then at 2.1k it was back to normal for some runs, so seems non-deterministic
[01:46] Maya Li: there's some heuristics plus actual microburst coupling with GC or infra noise. also note our sampling frequency can miss short spikes. that's why we recommended micro-sampling at 100ms granularity rather than 1s
[02:05] Priya Nair: we changed sampling to 100ms last night for a couple routes, results attached in the sheet but still noisy
[02:14] Ethan Park: quick question - are you running with KV cache enabled in dev? that will change the TTFT numbers a lot
[02:21] Tom Alvarez: on dev yes but only partial prefix caching, we didn't enable full prefix. last week we had concerns about memory footprint
[02:29] Maya Li: right, so the tradeoff: enable more aggressive KV caching and you reduce first-token time for repeat requests, but you need to accept higher memory usage or apply eviction policies. we shared a knob matrix in the doc
[02:44] Lea Wong: on quant, we tried 4-bit q (we labeled it q4f) and saw 10% less compute but also more variance at 99p
[02:52] Jordan Kim: yep quantization changes kernel selection too, sometimes the quant exec path uses a different GEMM kernel which is faster on throughput but has higher startup overhead
[03:04] Priya Nair: can you explain microburst? is it network or GPU scheduling?
[03:10] Santiago Ruiz: from our side looks like occasional preemption on the cluster but network egress also showed concurrent spikes the same time
[03:18] Maya Li: so we instrumented both. the microburst signature we see is 2-5x token latency for 200-800ms windows. often those align with GC cycles on some nodes or sudden mem pressure when KV cache gets warmed; sometimes also with multi-tenant eviction on the node
[03:36] Tom Alvarez: ok that matches our SRE notes. any immediate mitigations?
[03:41] Jordan Kim: a few: 1) pin high-priority routes to dedicated slots or dedicated capacity for the pilot; 2) reduce KV cache size and instead use sticky prefix caching for top N routes; 3) try the streaming handshake tweak — it lowers buffer latency at cost of some throughput
[04:00] Ethan Park: for the pilot we recommended sticky pinning on 10% nodes for heavy QPS routes, do you want us to try that in staging
[04:07] Tom Alvarez: yes please, can you provision sticky nodes on staging? we can mirror prod traffic shape for 2h window
[04:12] Ethan Park: noted
[04:14] Priya Nair: on tests we ran last night, the sticky nodes reduced 95p by about 22% but 99p only 12% — still some tail
[04:24] Maya Li: that's expected if the tail is infra noise. next is to combine sticky nodes + micro-sampling with higher resolution and prefix caching for the top 50 routes
[04:36] Lea Wong: question: how do we choose kernel sets? we've been seeing different kernels chosen for the same payloads across runs
[04:43] Jordan Kim: we have a kernel selector that considers sequence length distribution, batch size and quant profile. it can be forced too; for pilot we can lock to a kernel set as an experiment to measure deterministic behavior
[04:55] Tom Alvarez: locking sounds useful for debug but we're worried about losing throughput on big batches
[05:01] Maya Li: you can lock on a per-route basis and only for the debug window. then compare perf metrics to the dynamic selection baseline
[05:10] Priya Nair: action item: we want a short doc that explains tradeoffs between forcing kernel vs letting runtime pick, incl. perf delta numbers if available
[05:18] Ethan Park: Maya will prepare that, noted in action items
[05:22] Jordan Kim: also to mention, sometimes the runtime fallback is triggered by small batch sizes; if you can artificially batch or use continuous batching hints it may avoid the fallback
[05:33] Tom Alvarez: is continuous batching safe for our latency SLO?
[05:37] Maya Li: yes if configured with low max window and priority tiers, it can keep latency within SLO while getting throughput gains. we have config examples in the shared repo
[05:45] Priya Nair: can you attach example config?
[05:47] Ethan Park: will put configs in the drive after this call
[05:51] [06:00] Jordan Kim: switching to streaming variance, we saw handshake delays when stream buffer refill coincided with KV cache warmup. the handshake tweak reduces initial buffer allocation and smooths out refill cadence
[06:14] Santiago Ruiz: how invasive is that handshake change?
[06:18] Jordan Kim: minimal, a runtime flag. we tried it on 3 nodes in lab and saw fewer 100-200ms spikes in the stream path
[06:27] Lea Wong: any regression on throughput?
[06:29] Jordan Kim: small, 3-5% at high batch, so for query-per-second heavy routes maybe not ideal but for user-facing low-latency routes it helps
[06:38] Tom Alvarez: ok let's test handshake tweak + sticky nodes combo
[06:41] Maya Li: note on monitoring — please increase sampling resolution to 100ms for the pilot routes and export both client-side timing and kernel-level tracing. that helped us correlate the spikes to kernel flip events
[06:58] Priya Nair: we tried 100ms but our tracing agent collapsed at high throughput; need to coordinate sampling windows so we don't OOM the APM
[07:06] Ethan Park: recommended pattern: high-res sampling for narrow window (2-5mins) during controlled runs, then drop to 1s post-run. we can provide a script to orchestrate that
[07:18] Tom Alvarez: perfect
[07:20] [07:30] Maya Li: quick note about quantization: Q4F seemed promising for cost, but gave wider tail. suggested experiment: run q8 + per-route kernel forcing vs q4f dynamic to measure delta on TTFT and 99p
[07:44] Lea Wong: we can run those experiments, timeline?
[07:47] Ethan Park: aim for runs this week, results by Friday. please share any special payloads you think are representative
[07:55] Priya Nair: we have two heavy routes: /nlp/respond and /embed/bulk, will share payload sets
[08:02] Jordan Kim: also a housekeeping: please escalate any infra preemption events with node IDs so we can cross-reference with our runtime traces
[08:10] Santiago Ruiz: will do
[08:12] [08:20] Ethan Park: let's recap next steps and owners
[08:26] Priya Nair: recap good
[08:28] Ethan Park: recap: Maya to send kernel-forcing doc and q tradeoff note; Ethan to upload per-route CSV and sample traces; Tom to enable prefix KV on staging and run sticky node tests; HelixWorks to run q8 vs q4f matrix and share results by 2026-02-27; schedule deeper kernel selection meeting for Tue next week.
[08:52] Tom Alvarez: thanks all
[08:54] Maya Li: thanks, we'll follow up in the doc and update action items
[08:58] Priya Nair: thanks everyone

End of transcript.
